title: Install or recover Usher
summary: Install, verify, or recover the stateless Usher commands and matching Chancery selector through the Rust installer without changing semantic registration or any product runtime.
use_when: Usher should be installed, updated, inspected, verified, or recovered for the current macOS user.
do_not_use_when: Only membership should be reported; use usher.recognition.inspect.
A foreign selector should be adopted or another product should be changed.
outcome: A version-matched immutable release with coherent Usher CLI and provider selectors.
effects: Stages an immutable Usher release containing the recognition command, exact Rust installer and recovery executable, and matching provider bundle; holds product and catalog writer locks and advances owned command and provider selectors through one current release.
Inspection and verification are read-only. Installation and recovery change only Usher-owned local release artifacts and selectors; no service state or semantic registration is touched.
authority: Usher owns its release and selectors. Cell products retain all domain and declaration authority.
success: Recognition binary, installer, and provider versions match; exact candidate and retained release integrity checks pass; owned command and provider selectors follow one current release.
failure_and_recovery: Refuse foreign, tampered, stale, or unprovable selections. A failed publication restores the captured prior selectors when recovery can prove that basis.

Deliberate recovery uses a retained exact Rust package/install and a supported immutable release under the selected home. Restoring legacy manifest.txt releases detaches the owned public usher-install selector; inspection accepts that absence and the retained Rust executable can later reselect its release. The archived legacy deployer cannot recover from a new-format current release. Never edit retained release bytes.
privacy: The installer retains immutable executable and documentation releases and integrity manifests under the selected local home. It creates no domain database, retains no credentials or domain bodies, and makes no network or model call.
steps: Complete relevant development checks with ./ci.sh usher. Prepare both production executables with deployment/build.py; release and deployment assume prior CI success without rerunning CI or requiring a receipt.
Run usher-install install with the exact recognition binary, provider bundle, and optional expected current selection.

Use inspect and exact-candidate verify to establish installed identity, integrity, and coherent command/provider selection. Use retained verify-release and recover only against the exact intended supported release.
checkpoints: Version, integrity, ownership, and prior selection are established before advancing selectors.
Deployment creates no semantic project, database, worker, or schedule.
adaptation: Use --expected-current absent|releases/HASH to bind deployment to an observed selection. Use --home only for an intentional isolated or alternate-user boundary.
stop_when: A candidate or selector is foreign, stale, tampered, or cannot be restored coherently.
does_not_authorize: Release publication, foreign-selector takeover, retained-release deletion, or semantic registration.

interfaces.label: Install candidate
interfaces.invocation: usher-install install --binary ABSOLUTE_PATH --bundle ABSOLUTE_BUNDLE_PATH [--home ABSOLUTE_HOME] [--expected-current absent|releases/HASH]

consumers.statement: The current operator may install or recover Usher.

preconditions.statement: A version-matched candidate with verified source and executable integrity, and an owned coherent prior release/selector basis. Relevant development CI is expected beforehand but is not rerun or enforced by release or deployment preparation.

inputs.statement: Exact recognition binary, matching provider bundle and executing Rust installer, optional expected current and isolated home; verification or recovery selects an exact supported retained release directory.

outputs.statement: A version-matched immutable release with coherent Usher recognition, installer and provider selectors, or a read-only inspection or verification result.

data_semantics.statement: Release selectors establish installed bytes, not Cell membership or runtime readiness.

identity_and_units.statement: Product and provider versions, the cell-install-v1 manifest format, content-addressed release identity, adapter protocol version, capability contract version and recognition JSON schemas are separate axes.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: The operation covers the selected candidate and exact prior release basis.

access.statement: Current-user local filesystem through the separate Rust installer, bounded to product-owned release files and selectors; optional home is an explicit alternate or isolated boundary.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Product lock precedes catalog writer lock. An observed or explicit expected current selection prevents stale cutover. One atomic current selector selects both commands and documentation; failed publication restores the captured prior selectors when that basis is provable.

operational_limits.statement: No daemon, schedule, database, semantic registration, or other product runtime is operated.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Installation contract two uses the Rust installer CLI and cell-install-v1 JSON manifest with retained exact package/install recovery executable. Rust recovery supports legacy manifest.txt releases and detaches their unsupported public installer selector; the retained Rust executable remains available to reselect its release. The version-one coordinator adapter JSON protocol and recognition semantics remain unchanged.

reliances.statement: Installation uses the product-owned Rust executable and linked shared cell-install library. It does not require a Chancery executable, invoke represented systems, or delegate product authority to the deployment coordinator.
